t: Welcome to Claude Mastery from LetsVibeAI
Your instructor is Patrick Diamitani.
In this first lesson, you'll pick a harness and get it running in about 10 minutes.
You shift from typist to director, like a film director, describe what the scene needs,
then review and steer the AI's translation, not operate the camera.
A model is the brain. A harness is everything around it.
It reads your files, runs commands, calls tools, and remembers your rules.
Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and VS Code are all harnesses.
Under the hood, every harness has the same five layers.
The model, context, which is your rules and memory, capabilities, like skills and tool connections,
surfaces, meaning chat, terminal or editor, and orchestration, where agents work together.
Start with whatever you already use.
If you like the terminal, try Claude Code, Codex, or Hermes.
If you live in an editor, try VS Code, Cursor, or Antigravity.
Everything in this course carries over to all of them.
Make a fresh folder and turn it into a Git repo.
Git is your undo button.
Every change the agent makes can be reviewed and rolled back.
Then launch the harness inside that folder.
Here are three prompts to try on day one.
First, ask it to explain the folder.
Then ask for a plan and tell it not to write code yet.
Finally, ask it to do just step one, then stop.
Quick recap, a harness is the app around the model, and every harness shares the same five layers.
Your mission, install one harness, start a Git repo, and run the three day one prompts.
That's your setup.
Next lesson, we write the file that makes every session start smart.
Learn, build, ship with LetsVibeAI
